==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=lack of illness|:inh|enm:helthe<id:health>|tree=1|text=++}} Cognate with {{cog|goh|heilida}}. Analyzable as {{suffix|en|whole}}, {{m|en|hale}}, or {{suffix|en|heal|th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. More at {{m|en|heal}}. {{dbt|en|wholth}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|helth|helthe|healthe||obsolete}}

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ˈhɛlθ/|a=RP,GA}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-health.ogg|a=UK}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-health.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈhelθ/|a=AU,NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛlθ|s=1}}
* {{hmp|en|elf<aa:th-fronting,h-dropping>}}
* {{hyph|en|health}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|-|s}}

# The [[state]] of being free from [[physical]] or [[psychological]] [[disease]], [[illness]], or [[malfunction]]; [[wellness]]. {{defdate|from 11th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Her mental '''health''' is really affected by stressful environments.}}
#: {{ux|en|My grampa still enjoys very good '''health'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=4|passage=Then he commenced to talk, really talk. and inside of two flaps of a herring's fin he had me mesmerized, like Eben Holt's boy at the town hall show. He talked about the ills of humanity, and the glories of '''health''' and Nature and service and land knows what all.}}
# A [[state]] of [[well-being]] or [[balance]], often [[physical]] but sometimes also [[mental]] and [[social]]; the overall level of [[function]] of an [[organism]] from the cellular (micro) level to the social (macro) level.
#: {{ux|en|The directors are concerned about the financial '''health''' of the project.}}
# Physical [[condition]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[cure|Cure]], [[remedy]]. {{defdate|16th c. (Middle English: 11th|15th c.)}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A [[toast]] to [[prosperity]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
# {{senseid|en|video games}}{{lb|en|video games}} The amount of damage an in-game entity can withstand before it is killed, destroyed or defeated.
#: {{ux|en|The enemies on this level have a lot of '''health'''.}}
#* {{quote-web|en
|date=March 6 2018|title=Dispelling the myths of Bloodborne|author=Martin Robinson|work=Eurogamer|passage=Lose a little '''health''' and there's a few seconds in which you'll be able to win it back by ragging on an enemy.
|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2018-03-06-dispelling-the-myths-of-bloodborne
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260310063605/https://www.eurogamer.net/dispelling-the-myths-of-bloodborne}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=[[w:PC Gamer|PC Gamer (US)]]|date=February 2025|number=392|page=91|title=Reinstall: ''Path of Exile''|author=Tyler Colp
|text=Enemies can knock your '''health''' down to zero if you're not careful and item upgrades are slow to come by.}}

===Etymology 2===
{{etymon|en|id=warrior}}
From {{inh|en|enm|heleð||man, hero, fighter}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hæleþ||man, hero, fighter}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*haliþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*haliþaz||man, hero}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|held||hero}}, {{cog|nl|held||hero}}, {{cog|de|Held||hero}}, {{cog|nn|hauld||freeman}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[warrior]]; [[hero]]; [[man]].
#* {{RQ:Drayton Poly-Olbion|text=They, under false pretence of amity and cheer, the British peers invite, the German '''healths''' to view.}}
